data.why: The repo's only example dataset (paper/data/ggir_outputs/output_sub001) stores its GGIR .RData/.png files via git-lfs, which this sandbox cannot fetch; the app only parses those .RData files when a subject is missing from its SQLite cache, so the seed script builds output_sub001/actigraphy.sqlite directly (4 days of 5-minute-epoch anglez/ENMO data with a night, a nap, and a non-wear gap) so 'Load Files' works without git-lfs.

goals: Load a participant's GGIR output folder (select output_sub001 from the dropdown and click Load Files) and step through each night's actigraphy trace.
Drag the sleep-window slider under the graph to correct a night's onset/offset and see the change persist in the Sleep Times table.
Flag a night that needs further review, and flag a night with more than 2 hours of missing wear data between 8PM-8AM.
Click Add Slider to mark a second sleep window (nap or extra nocturnal awakening) on a day that has one, then Remove Slider to delete it.
Move through all selectable nights for the subject and confirm the app writes data_cleaning, multiple_sleep, and sleeplog CSVs under output_sub001/logs/.

review.summary: The goal, phases and features match the README's workflow for correcting GGIR sleep windows, and 8 of the 9 screens I sampled fully show what their nodes claim. Before filing, it needs to say that the missing-data switch and empty nights exclude nights from analysis, end on the output files rather than on a reload test, and record the stale graph in screens/031.webp.
